articles.title: AICTE extends Industry Fellowship Programme 2026-27 registration deadline to October 31: Check complete details here
articles.summary: The All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) has extended the registration deadline for Phase 2 of the Industry Fellowship Programme (IFP)
articles.body: The All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) has extended the registration deadline for Phase 2 of the Industry Fellowship Programme (IFP) 2026-27 to October 31, 2026. Eligible industries and organisations interested in participating in the initiative can now complete their registration through the official portal, ifp.aicte.gov.in.The programme is aimed at strengthening collaboration between technical institutions and industry partners, with a focus on making academic learning more aligned with workplace requirements. Through the initiative, AICTE seeks to provide greater industry exposure, encourage practical skill development and promote innovation through closer engagement between educational institutions and employers.Organisations planning to participate in Phase 2 must complete the registration process within the revised timeline and ensure that they meet the eligibility conditions prescribed by the council.What is the AICTE Industry Fellowship Programme?The Industry Fellowship Programme is an AICTE initiative designed to bridge the gap between classroom education and the practical requirements of the industrial sector. It seeks to establish stronger connections between academic institutions and organisations, allowing students and professionals to gain a better understanding of industry practices and workplace challenges.The programme also aims to encourage industry participation in applied research, innovation and technical education. By facilitating interactions between industry representatives and academic institutions, AICTE intends to make teaching and learning more responsive to changing technological developments and employer expectations.The initiative is particularly relevant at a time when industries are increasingly seeking graduates with practical experience, technical proficiency and familiarity with emerging technologies.AICTE IFP 2026-27: Eligibility criteria for participating organisationsAICTE has prescribed specific eligibility conditions for industries and organisations seeking to register under the Industry Fellowship Programme 2026-27. Applicants must fulfil the following requirements:Indian registration: The organisation must have a registered office in India.Operational experience: The organisation must have been operational for at least five years.Annual turnover: It must have recorded an average annual turnover of Rs 100 crore or more during the preceding three financial years.The programme is open to different categories of business entities, including proprietorships, partnerships, private limited companies, public limited companies and public sector undertakings (PSUs).However, organisations belonging to these categories must also satisfy the prescribed registration, operational and financial requirements to qualify for participation.How to register for AICTE Industry Fellowship Programme 2026-27Eligible industries and organisations can complete the registration process online through the official AICTE Industry Fellowship Programme portal. Applicants can follow these steps:Visit the official website at ifp.aicte.gov.in.Access the industry registration section available on the portal.Enter the required organisational details and other information specified by AICTE.Complete the registration formalities as instructed on the website.Review the submitted information and complete the onboarding process within the prescribed deadline.Organisations are advised to check the eligibility conditions and keep the necessary details ready before starting the application process to avoid last-minute difficulties.AICTE's focus on strengthening industry-academia collaborationThe Industry Fellowship Programme is part of AICTE's broader efforts to increase industry participation in technical education. The council aims to create a more direct relationship between academic institutions and employers so that students can develop skills that are relevant to actual workplace requirements.Traditional classroom-based learning may not always provide sufficient exposure to the practical challenges encountered in industrial settings. Closer institutional partnerships can help address this gap by encouraging industry-oriented learning, applied research and knowledge exchange.Through the fellowship initiative, AICTE seeks to create opportunities for organisations to contribute more actively to technical education while enabling academic institutions to understand changing industry expectations.With the Phase 2 registration deadline now extended to October 31, eligible organisations have until the revised date to complete the process through the official portal.Get the latest Education News and Live updates. articles.title: She turned abandoned slum walls into classrooms across 100+ communities; Mumbai artist Rouble Nagi wins the $1 million Global Teacher Prize 2026
articles.summary: An abandoned wall in a neighbourhood rarely attracts much attention.
articles.body: An abandoned wall in a neighbourhood rarely attracts much attention. But for Indian artist and educator Rouble Nagi, it can become a classroom, a learning resource and a starting point for a child's education. Over the past two decades, she has transformed neglected walls into interactive educational murals, using art to bring learning closer to children in underserved communities.Nagi has now been named the winner of the $1 million GEMS Education Global Teacher Prize 2026, an initiative of the Varkey Foundation organised in collaboration with UNESCO. Her name was announced at the World Governments Summit in Dubai, where she was selected from more than 5,000 nominations and applications representing 139 countries. Now in its tenth year, the award is among the largest global recognitions for educators.From neglected walls to open-air classroomsAt the centre of Nagi's work is her concept of 'Living Walls of Learning'. Through this initiative, broken and abandoned walls are converted into large-scale educational murals that introduce children to subjects such as literacy, numeracy, science, hygiene, history and environmental awareness.The murals are designed as interactive learning spaces rather than decorative artwork. They encourage children to explore concepts visually and make learning accessible in neighbourhoods where conventional educational infrastructure may be limited.Through the Rouble Nagi Art Foundation (RNAF), she has established more than 800 learning centres across over 100 underserved communities and villages in India. These centres provide children who have never attended school with opportunities to begin structured learning and eventually enter the formal education system. They also offer remedial support, creative activities and a safe learning environment to children already enrolled in schools.Over the years, her initiatives have helped bring more than one million children into the formal education system. Nagi has also recruited and trained over 600 volunteer and paid educators to work across the foundation's learning centres.Making education accessible to marginalised childrenNagi's work addresses challenges that often prevent children from attending school, including poverty, child labour, early marriage, irregular attendance and inadequate infrastructure. Her approach takes these circumstances into account while designing learning programmes.The centres follow flexible schedules to accommodate children who work or have household responsibilities. Lessons also use recycled materials and hands-on activities to explain concepts, allowing children to participate without depending on expensive educational resources.According to the foundation, its programmes have reduced dropout rates by more than 50% and improved long-term school retention. Nagi also travels across India to work with children and mentor educators who lead the centres.Sunny Varkey, founder of the Global Teacher Prize, GEMS Education and the Varkey Foundation, said Nagi's work demonstrated how creativity and commitment could help bring education to marginalised communities. UNESCO Assistant Director-General for Education Stefania Giannini also congratulated her, highlighting the role of teachers in helping children access education and build opportunities for their future.Plans for a skilling instituteNagi plans to use the $1 million prize money to establish a Skilling Institute that will provide free vocational and digital literacy training to marginalised children and young people. The proposed institute is intended to extend her work beyond foundational education and provide access to practical skills.Her work in education runs alongside an established career in art and urban renewal. Through the Rouble Nagi Art Foundation and Rouble Nagi Design Studio, she has created more than 850 murals and sculptures and participated in over 200 exhibitions worldwide.A member of the India Design Council, Nagi was the first artist invited to exhibit at the Rashtrapati Bhavan Museum. Her work has also been selected for the President of India's permanent collection. Among her other recognitions are the Jijamata Award, GR8 Award, MAP Noble Artist Award and HELLO! articles.title: La casa encantada de Valencia: el primer "poltergeist" reconocido de España, fechado en 1915
articles.standfirst: En un edificio de la plaza de l’Espart de la capital valenciana
articles.summary: En un edificio de la plaza de l’Espart de la capital valenciana
articles.body: Halloween está ya. Hoy es 31 de octubre, la noche de las tinieblas... y siempre hay casos llamativos de situaciones paranormales que mitifican más si cabe una noche como la de hoy. Uno de los casos más llamativos es el considerado primer 'poltergeist' reconocido. A principios del siglo XX, un extraño fenómeno mantuvo en vilo a toda Valencia. Golpes inexplicables que resonaban día y noche, investigaciones oficiales sin respuestas y cientos de curiosos congregados en torno a una vivienda del centro histórico alimentaron una historia que aún hoy sigue envuelta en el misterio. Todo ocurrió en la plaza de l’Espart, en pleno barrio del Mercat y a escasos metros de la plaza del Tossal, en la capital valenciana. Corría junio de 1915 cuando los vecinos comenzaron a escuchar unos fuertes golpes procedentes del entresuelo de una casa en la que residían un excapitán de la Guardia Civil y sus dos hijos. Los ruidos eran tan intensos que se escuchaban perfectamente desde la propia plaza e incluso desde calles cercanas. La expectación creció a tal velocidad que los guardias municipales tuvieron que vigilar el edificio y controlar a las personas que acudían para intentar descubrir el origen de aquel fenómeno. Durante semanas, Valencia no habló de otra cosa. La popularidad del caso llegó a tal punto que los ciegos copleros que recorrían las calles con sus organillos empezaron a cantar canciones inspiradas en la conocida ya como "casa misteriosa". Lejos de desaparecer, los golpes fueron aumentando en intensidad. La multitud que se concentraba frente al inmueble, entre la curiosidad y el miedo, obligó a las autoridades a acordonar la zona para evitar incidentes. La vivienda recibió entonces un apodo que hizo fortuna entre los valencianos: la casa de Tocame Roque. Mientras tanto, parte de la prensa de la época apuntaba a una explicación sobrenatural y comenzó a hablar del supuesto responsable de los sucesos: un espíritu o duende que acabaría dando nombre al caso, el Donyet de la plaza de l’Espart. Tal fue la magnitud del fenómeno que provocó incluso la intervención de la Justicia. Arquitectos municipales y provinciales, además de decenas de agentes y técnicos, participaron en una investigación que intentó aclarar qué estaba ocurriendo realmente. Se realizaron perforaciones en el inmueble, escuchas mediante micrófonos en paredes y barandillas, inspecciones del alcantarillado y hasta una conexión telefónica con una vivienda cercana de la calle Caballeros para tratar de localizar la procedencia de los ruidos. Sin embargo, tras semanas de pruebas, nadie fue capaz de ofrecer una explicación convincente. Con el paso de los años surgió una hipótesis que muchos investigadores consideran la más probable. Según esta versión, el propietario de una vivienda colindante mantenía un conflicto con el dueño de la casa afectada por una medianera compartida. El objetivo habría sido adquirir el inmueble para ampliar considerablemente su propiedad. Ante la imposibilidad de llegar a un acuerdo, se especula con que pudo intentar asustar a la familia simulando que la vivienda estaba encantada mediante golpes provocados de forma intencionada. Nunca se pudo demostrar. Lo que sí quedó para siempre es el recuerdo de un episodio único en la historia de Valencia. El caso del Donyet de la plaza de l’Espart está considerado por muchos investigadores como el primer "poltergeist" documentado oficialmente en España, ya que movilizó a las autoridades y dio pie a una investigación pública que jamás logró resolver el enigma.

articles.title: Alexmay Valladares, la entrenadora personal venezolana de 27 años que ha cautivado al multimillonario José Elías
articles.standfirst: Anuncian su compromiso casi cinco años después de conocerse y empezar una relación
articles.summary: Anuncian su compromiso casi cinco años después de conocerse y empezar una relación
articles.body: El empresario catalán José Elías vuelve a saltar a la palestra, pero en este caso no por su negocios. En esta ocasión, ha anunciado su compromiso con Alexmay Valladares, una entrenadora personal venezolana de 27 años con la que mantiene una relación desde finales de 2021. El multimillonario tiene 50 años y se lleva 23 con respecto a su mujer. Ha sido precisamente esta última la que ha escrito a través de la cuenta de instagram la buen nueva y su sentimiento. "Mil veces sí", escribía la joven, que también ha dedicado unas palabras a su futuro marido: "Te elegiría una y mil veces más". Alexmay Valladares es una modelo y entrenadora personal venezolana que vive en España desde 2019. Se dedica a la creación de contenido relacionado con el deporte y la nutrición, pero también ha trabajado como auxiliar administrativa en Audax Renovables, que es una de las empresas más importantes de su pareja. Tanto Elías como Valladares iniciaron una relación en 2021. Concretamente en diciembre de ese año y desde entonces han compartido numerosos viajes a lo largo del planeta solidificando dicha relación que les ha llevado al compromiso anunciado. Elías es un afamado empresario catalán que cuenta con empresas como Audax Renovables y La Sirena que han supuesto un gran aumento de capital en el empresario dada su audacia en la materia. Para él será su segundo matrimonio, ya que Elías estuvo casado previamente y es padre de tres hijos.

articles.title: Protests outside Poland’s constitutional court: What’s the crisis about?
articles.summary: Poland’s centrist government says it is restoring judicial independence after years of far-right political interference.
articles.body:
Riot police have been deployed outside Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal as a dispute over who should serve on the court escalates into a confrontation between Prime Minister Donald Tusk’s government and the nationalist opposition.

Hundreds of protesters gathered outside the Warsaw building on Friday night after judges elected by the current parliamentary majority announced the suspension of the tribunal’s president, Bogdan Swieczkowski, and his deputy, Bartlomiej Sochanski.

The move drew condemnation from the far-right opposition Law and Justice party, known as PiS, and prompted President Karol Nawrocki, a PiS ally, to abandon a trip to Senegal, turning his plane around to return to Poland on Friday. Police said three people were arrested after trying to enter the court complex.

Tusk says decisive action is necessary to restore the rule of law after years of political interference in the Constitutional Tribunal under PiS. Here is what we know.

Why are Poland’s leaders fighting over the Constitutional Tribunal?

The Constitutional Tribunal decides whether laws comply with Poland’s constitution. Its rulings can prevent legislation from taking effect, making its independence and who sits on its bench politically significant.

This latest dispute can be traced back to 2015, during the transfer of power from a centrist government led by Tusk’s Civic Platform party to the far-right PiS.

The outgoing parliament elected five judges, although Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal subsequently found that only three of those appointments had a valid legal basis. The incoming PiS majority then elected replacements, including for the three seats already lawfully filled. Then-President Andrzej Duda refused to swear in the three validly elected judges.

During its eight years in government, PiS introduced broader judicial changes that critics said brought the courts under greater political influence. PiS is currently the main opposition in Poland.

“It was a power play to control who serves as a justice, in what positions, and how the court system operates in Poland,” Wojciech Przybylski, editor-in-chief of Visegrad Insight, told Al Jazeera.

“The former PiS government wanted a court system and tribunal that would allow it to pass laws that supported their ideological perspective. It also wanted control of a Constitutional Tribunal that would support its claim of sovereignty over the EU.”

Aleksandra Kustra-Rogatka, an associate professor at Nicolaus Copernicus University in Torun, told Al Jazeera that “after Przylebska became president of the CC, the rule of law crisis worsened. Controversial laws reformed the judicial system, and the court became seen as a rubber-stamp body and an active political player supporting illiberal policies.”

The European Court of Human Rights, which is separate from the EU, had already ruled in 2021 that an improperly appointed judge’s participation deprived a company of its right to a tribunal established by law. Then, in December 2025, the EU’s highest court ruled that the tribunal had not met the requirements of an independent court. It also found that tribunal judgements challenging the authority of EU law breached Poland’s obligations as a member state.

Tusk returned to office as prime minister in December 2023 promising to restore judicial independence, and his government has refused to recognise the tribunal’s legitimacy in its existing form and has been attempting to disregard its rulings.

Kustra-Rogatka added that “many supporters of the centrist governing camp have grown disappointed by the lack of progress in restoring the rule of law since 2023, partly constrained by the prospect of losing the 2025 presidential election”.

This year, the parliament elected eight judges to the 15-member tribunal. President Nawrocki, a supporter of Donald Trump, was elected last year and with the power to veto legislation, administered the oath to three judges but withheld it from five, who instead took their oaths without his presence. The tribunal’s president, Bogdan Swieczkowski, refused to allow those five to begin adjudicating.

What triggered the latest confrontation?

On Friday, Judge Anna Korwin-Piotrowska announced one-month suspensions of court president Swieczkowski and his deputy, Sochanski, and said she was assuming responsibility for running the tribunal.

But questions have arisen over whether Korwin-Piotrowska, who is one of the court’s 15 justices alongside Swieczkowski and Sochanski, has the authority to do this. Her claim rests on her length of judicial service overall, rather than having served longest on the tribunal.

In separate measures, Justice Minister Waldemar Zurek, who also serves as prosecutor general, took steps that could lead to criminal proceedings against the suspended president, Swieczkowski, and his deputy, Sochanski. Far-right critics say these measures are politically motivated and intended to apply pressure on the already suspended justices.

PiS supporters, including senior party figures, gathered outside to oppose the suspensions on Friday. Police said their deployment followed information from Korwin-Piotrowska about possible threats to judges and staff and risks to public order. They said officers were securing the grounds and had not entered the tribunal building.

Nawrocki turned back to Poland midair while flying to Senegal and arrived at the tribunal during the night. By Saturday morning, he had called urgent consultations with parliamentary representatives, describing events as a forcible takeover of a constitutional institution.

Tusk defended the effort to restore the rule of law, saying that reversing the legacy of PiS required difficult action.

The confrontation raises two overlapping questions: who is entitled to sit on the tribunal, and whether the measures used to change its leadership are lawful.

Marcin Matczak, a prominent Polish lawyer, told Al Jazeera that the far-right opposition was defending its “remaining institutional stronghold”, while the centrist government wants to “restore balance to the Constitutional Tribunal”.

But restoring independence also requires scrutiny of the current government’s choices. In September, its parliamentary majority elected Maciej Berek, previously a minister in Tusk’s cabinet, to the tribunal. Some coalition members opposed the appointment, saying it contradicted promises to depoliticise the judiciary.

With parliamentary elections due next year, Matczak said Tusk might be taking a harder line to mobilise supporters frustrated by the slow pace of reform. “But that is a risky strategy: it may energise his political base while alienating more moderate voters,” he said.

A more immediate flashpoint could be a tribunal judges’ meeting that Matczak said had been called for November 3. Attempts to lift immunity could deepen the confrontation if the assembly’s composition or ability to reach the required quorum is challenged.

Matczak also warned that the scenes could establish a precedent for future governments. “A future government could invoke these events to argue that sending the police into the Constitutional Tribunal is an acceptable way to resolve a legal dispute,” he said.

“Whatever the immediate political gains, the long-term institutional consequences could be deeply damaging.”

articles.title: Muere Marisa Manchado, compositora y Premio Nacional de Música, en el accidente ferroviario de Urda
articles.standfirst: La artista madrileña, de 70 años, viajaba a Sevilla para participar en un encuentro dedicado a su trayectoria.
articles.summary: La artista madrileña, de 70 años, viajaba a Sevilla para participar en un encuentro dedicado a su trayectoria.
articles.body: El accidente ferroviario de Urda (Toledo) se ha cobrado la vida de Marisa Manchado, compositora, pianista y musicóloga española, a los 70 años. La noticia ha provocado una profunda conmoción en el mundo cultural, donde era reconocida tanto por su extensa producción artística como por su compromiso con la visibilidad de las mujeres en la música. Manchado viajaba en uno de los trenes siniestrados rumbo a Sevilla, donde tenía previsto participar en un encuentro organizado por la Facultad de Ciencias de la Educación de la Universidad hispalense para analizar su obra. La Asociación Madrileña de Compositores, de la que fue socia fundadora y primera presidenta, ha confirmado su fallecimiento y ha trasladado sus condolencias a familiares y allegados. Nacida en Madrid en 1956, Marisa Manchado desarrolló una carrera de más de cuatro décadas en la que compuso más de 150 obras de distintos géneros, desde música de cámara y piezas sinfónicas hasta composiciones vocales, electroacústicas y operísticas. En 2024 recibió el Premio Nacional de Música en la modalidad de composición por su ópera 'La Regenta', basada en la novela de Leopoldo Alas, Clarín, con libreto de Amelia Valcárcel. La obra, estrenada en 2023 en una coproducción del Teatro Real y el Teatro Español, fue también candidata a los International Opera Awards. Entre sus trabajos más destacados figura 'El cristal de agua fría', con libreto de la escritora Rosa Montero, con quien mantuvo una estrecha colaboración artística. Más allá de su faceta como compositora, Manchado fue una figura fundamental en la defensa de la igualdad dentro del ámbito musical. En 1982 fundó el programa 'Mujeres en la Música' de Radio 2 y publicó en 1998 el ensayo 'Música y mujeres, género y poder', considerado una obra de referencia sobre la situación de las mujeres en este sector. También ocupó la Subdirección General de Música y Danza del INAEM entre 2007 y 2008 y fue durante 14 años vicedirectora del Conservatorio Profesional de Música Teresa Berganza de Madrid. Su fallecimiento supone una pérdida para la cultura española y, especialmente, para la música contemporánea, a la que dedicó toda su vida.
